subject: biology-1
question: A researcher uses freeze-fracture electron microscopy on a **plasma membrane** and observes membrane proteins scattered unevenly through the lipid layer, with their positions changing over time. Which model of membrane structure best explains this observation?

options.text: The fluid mosaic model, in which a fluid bilayer holds a mobile mosaic of proteins that can drift.
The sandwich model, in which rigid protein layers coat both sides of the lipid core.
The pore model, in which proteins are fixed in permanent channels that never move.
The scaffolding model, in which lipids are locked in place on a fixed protein frame.

explanation: The fluid mosaic model describes the membrane as a fluid bilayer in which proteins move laterally through the lipid, which matches the scattered, shifting proteins the researcher observed. The sandwich, pore, and scaffolding models all treat membrane proteins as fixed in place, so none of them can explain proteins that drift.
